newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May existing home sales rose 4.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May existing home sales rose 4.4 pct.

text.p: Sales of existing U.S. homes rose 4.4 percent in May to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.24 million units from 4.06 million units in April, the National Association of Realtors said Wednesday.
Wall Street economists had forecast May sales of 4.07 million units.
The May sales rate was down 0.9 percent from sales of 4.28 million in May last year.

"Given the robust activity earlier this year, we had expected sales to ease off. But the current volume reflects sustained consumer confidence, strong employment figures and some pent-up demand in the trade-up market," NAR President Russell Booth said.
"Although we are well into a period of very strong housing activity, we expect fairly stable sales for the balance of the year," he said.
The May resale rate was 0.9 percent below the record set in May 1996, when it was 4.28 million units.
